API QA Tester Summary - Issue #963: Implement New Plunk 0.4.0

Suite: qa_testing/scripts/run-issue-963-live-api.cjs
Live API: https://apil.gothru.co
Related FE: gothru-dashboard auth email flows
Env: Production API with real tester account testpanorra@gmail.com; sensitive token/link values redacted.

Result

Partial Pass / Needs Follow-up.

The main dashboard auth email path is wired to the new Plunk sender and a real production request returned 200 Email sent. However, source review still found direct legacy-style PLUNK_API / PLUNK_API_KEY calls in several payment/support helper paths, so the implementation is not fully centralized on the new EmailClass / USEPLUNK_* contract.

FE -> BE Flow Mapping

FE source FE API call Method Payload Headers / options
gothru-dashboard/src/pages/Auth/ForgotPassword.jsx /auth/forgot-password POST { email, redirect_url: window.location.origin + '/change-password' } JSON, x-localization, withCredentials: true
gothru-dashboard/src/components/organism/UngroupedComp/ResendEmailButtons.jsx /auth/forgot-password POST { email: forgotPasswordEmail, redirect_url } JSON, x-localization
gothru-dashboard/src/components/organism/UngroupedComp/ResendEmailButtons.jsx /v1/auth/resend-verification POST { email: registerEmail, redirect_url, tour } JSON, x-localization
gothru-dashboard/src/pages/Auth/Register.jsx /v1/users/register POST { email, password, first_name, last_name, redirect_url, newslatter, tour? } JSON, x-localization, withCredentials: true

Dashboard base URL source: REACT_APP_BASE_URL = https://apil.gothru.co.

BE Route / Action / Email Contract

Route Controller / action Email sender Plunk payload contract
POST /auth/forgot-password Auth\AuthController@forgotPassword -> Auth\Actions\ForgotPassword App\Class\EmailClass::send() { to, template, data }
POST /v1/auth/resend-verification Auth\AuthController@resendEmailVerifyV1 -> Auth\Actions\ResendEmailVerify App\Class\EmailClass::send() { to, template, data }
POST /v1/users/register User\Register\V1\RegisterControllerV1@registerUserV1 -> RegisterUserV1 App\Class\EmailClass::send() { to, template, data }

EmailClass uses:

  • USEPLUNK_URL
  • USEPLUNK_SECRET_KEY
  • Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
  • Content-Type: application/json

Code Review Summary

Pass:

  • app/Class/EmailClass.php implements the new reusable sender with USEPLUNK_URL, USEPLUNK_SECRET_KEY, bearer auth, JSON payload, HTTP status capture, and success flag.
  • Forgot password, resend verification, and V1 register email flows call EmailClass::send() with template UUIDs and template data.
  • POST /auth/forgot-password was verified with real production API data and returned 200 Email sent.

Needs follow-up:

  • Direct PLUNK_API / PLUNK_API_KEY calls still exist in:
    • app/Http/Controllers/User/UserController.php
    • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Helpers/Subscription/UpgradeHelper.php
    • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Helpers/OneTimePayment/UnlockOverlayPublicHelpers.php
  • Some payment helpers now route through EmailClass::send() but still pass event-style names in places; template UUID vs event-name usage should be confirmed against Plunk 0.4.0 expectations.
  • POST /v1/auth/resend-verification does not validate empty email before DB lookup and returns Email already exist, which is confusing for invalid input. Not the main Plunk migration blocker, but worth cleaning up.

True Negative 2 Invalid forgot-password email rejected, resend negative request rejected

False Negative 1 Remaining direct PLUNK_API usages mean full migration is not complete

Conclusion

Issue #963 is partially implemented. The dashboard auth email flow is working with the new Plunk sender on production, but the repository still contains legacy/direct Plunk calls that should be migrated or explicitly marked out of scope before this issue is considered fully complete.

Bug Report

Item Detail
Confirmed bug GET /sv/info/{mid} returns inconsistent success data shape for real moderation IDs.
Main impact FE Status.jsx expects res.data to be an array and calls .map(). Several real moderation IDs return { "message": "null" } with HTTP 200, which is not FE-compatible.
Secondary issue A nonexistent moderation ID also returns HTTP 200 with { "message": "invalid moderation ID" }, so invalid input is reported as success.
Direct retest proof Retested manually with GET https://apil.gothru.co/sv/info/3544123; response was 200 OK with { "statusCode": 200, "data": { "message": "null" } }.
Expected behavior Success response should consistently return an array of "<id> - <color>"; invalid or unavailable moderation should return a controlled non-2xx/empty-array contract agreed with FE.
Actual behavior 5 of 10 real moderation IDs returned data as object, not array. Nonexistent moderation returned 200.

issues.display_title: Issue #1606: Fix Bug "Failed to upload avatar" Error on Photographer Profile for New Accounts
issues.main_description_html:
Description

Users with newly created accounts are unable to upload a logo/avatar on their Photographer Profile page. When attempting to drag and drop or click to upload an image into the designated area, the upload fails and triggers a red toast notification stating: "Failed to upload avatar".

User Notes & Workaround Attempt

The user suspected the account might need an initial activity trigger to initialize storage space, so they tried creating a virtual tour and successfully uploaded a 360 image to that tour. However, returning to the profile page and attempting the avatar upload still resulted in the exact same failure.

Test File Used

A standard 360 view logo (PNG/JPG) was used for the upload attempt, ruling out an obscure file type issue.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. New accounts can successfully upload an avatar/logo to their profile immediately after registration.
  2. The avatar upload process functions independently and does not require the user to create a tour or perform other actions to "unlock" or initialize their storage.
  3. If an upload fails due to validation (size/format), the UI displays a clear and accurate reason to the user.

Test Scenario (for Tester / QA)

Preconditions

  • Have (or create) a brand-new account that has performed no other activity (no tours, no uploads).
  • Open browser DevTools -> Network/Console to capture the failing avatar upload request/response.
  • Have a valid avatar image ready (standard PNG/JPG within allowed size).

Scenario 1 - Fresh account avatar upload (the bug)

  1. Register a new account and go directly to Photographer Profile.
  2. Upload an avatar/logo via drag-and-drop and again via click-to-upload.
  3. Expected: The avatar uploads successfully and displays on the profile - no "Failed to upload avatar" toast.
  4. Bug (before fix): Red toast "Failed to upload avatar" appears; avatar is not saved.

Scenario 2 - No tour-creation dependency

  1. On a fresh account that has never created a tour, upload the avatar first (before any other action).
  2. Expected: Upload works without needing to create a tour or upload a 360 image first (the storage-init workaround must not be required).

Scenario 3 - Persistence after reload

  1. After a successful avatar upload, reload the profile page (and re-login).
  2. Expected: The avatar persists and is shown consistently.

Scenario 4 - Validation error messaging

  1. Attempt to upload an oversized file and an unsupported format (e.g. .bmp/.svg/.txt).
  2. Expected: Upload is rejected with a clear, accurate reason (e.g. "File too large (max X MB)" / "Unsupported format - use PNG or JPG") - not a generic "Failed to upload avatar".

Scenario 5 - Update existing avatar

  1. Upload a new avatar to replace an existing one.
  2. Expected: The new image replaces the old one successfully.

Scenario 6 - Regression on established accounts

  1. Repeat the avatar upload on an older/established account.
  2. Expected: Still works - the fix doesn't regress accounts that already worked.

Pass criteria: A brand-new account can upload an avatar immediately with no workaround; failures only occur for genuine validation issues and show a clear, specific message.

Reference: docs/superpowers/specs/analyze-all.md - see section 3 Persona A (Photographer) and section 4 (Photographer profile & directory).
